 Member, Prl. M.A.C.T., Bengaluru.

 No.27, 5th cross road,

 Chartered Beverly hills,

 Bangalore - 560 061.

* * *
 JUDGMENT Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a road traffic accident filed petition under Sec.163-A of I.M.V. Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents who are insurer and owner of the Car No. KA-05-MW-0304 asserting that on 27.01.2019 at about 9.30 PM when travelling by sitting on the pillion of the motorcycle No.KA-01-JB-5560 from Magadi road towards Sompura on NICE Road, near Kengeri Exit Toll, Kengeri, driver of Car No. KA-05-MW-0304 drove the same in same direction overtake the motorcycle on the right side turned towards left dashed the car to the motorcycle thereby caused accident caused injuries to the petitioner.
2. Petitioner took treatment at Mathru Hospital and Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru at the cost of Rs.1,50,000/-.
3. As on the date of the accident petitioner being aged 30 years use to earn Rs.40,000/- per annum by working as coolie .
4. Regarding the accident Kengeri Traffic Police registered Crime No.13/2019 against the driver of Car for having committed the offence punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
5.

In response to the notice, the respondent No.1 and 2 appeared through their respective Advocates and filed separate written statements denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of the accident,
nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner, age, income and occupation of the petitioner.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 08.08.2023 this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a Motor Vehicle Accident that occurred on 27.1.2019 at about 9.30 p.m., when he was travelling as pillion rider in his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.01-JB-5560 and was hit by the car bearing registration No.KA-05-MW- 0304?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order?
7. On 23.03.2023, 02.06.2023,, 04.07.2023 petitioner deposed as PW.1 and produced 10 documents at Exs.P.1 to P.10.

On 20.06.2023, 14.07.2023, petitioner produced evidence of Dr. B.N. Nagaraj as Swamy vs Pradeep Kumar.K on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55407070/
2 PW.2 and get produced 2 documents at Exhibits P.11 to P.12.
8.
I heard the arrangement submitted on behalf of petitioner and respondent No.1 and perused the records.

9. On the basis of the materials placed on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1...
In the Affirmative, Issue No.2...
Petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.2,11,100/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., as compensation, Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:-

In the evidence affidavit, petitioner has stated that on 27.01.2019 at about 9.30 PM when travelling by sitting on the pillion of the motorcycle No.KA- 01-JB-5560 from Magadi road towards Sompura on NICE Road, near Kengeri Exit Toll, Kengeri, driver of Car No. KA- 05-MW-0304 which was running in the same direction overtook the motorcycle from the right side suddenly turned towards left without furnishing signal made the car to dash to the motorcycle thereby caused accident caused injuries to the petitioner.
11. In the written statements, respondent No.1 and 2 denied the allegation regarding the reason and mode of accident.
12. In the cross-examination made on behalf of the respondent No.2, PW.1 admitted that police have filed chargesheet against the rider of the motorcycle in which he was a pillion rider.
As the petition has been filed u/S 163-A of the IMV Act, consideration of the negligence does not arise.
13. In the evidence, PW.2 stated nothing regarding reason and mode of the accident.

14. Ex.P1 is the copy of FIR pertaining to Crime No.13/2019 registered by Kengeri Traffic Police against the rider of motorcycle No.KA-01-JB-5160 (Thimmegowda) for having committed the offence punishable under Section 283 & 337 of IPC, on the basis of the complaint filed by respondent No.1 Pradeep Kumar K, the driver of the car.
Ex.P2 is the copy of the spot mahazar.

Ex.P3 is the copy of the sketch of the place of accident in which it is noted that in the junction of the two roads, collision taken place between Car No.KA-05-MW-0304 motorcycle No. KA-01- JB-5560 which was running in the same direction (North to South).
15.
Ex.P4 is the copy of the Motor Vehicle Accident Report.

Ex.P5 is the copy of the chargesheet filed by Kengeri Traffic police in crime No.13/2019 against Pradeep S/o Thimmegowda, the driver of the Car No. KA-05-MW- 0304 for having committed offence punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.,
Sec.13(A&B), 187 of IMV Act.
16.

In this case, at this stage, there are no dispute regarding the involvement of the vehicle No.
KA-01-JB- 5560 and KA-05-MW-0304 in the accident resulting in the injuries to the petitioner.
Swamy vs Pradeep Kumar.K on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55407070/
3

Hence, I have concluded that on 27.07.2019 at 9.30 PM on Magadi Road towards Sompura Road on NICE Road Junction/NICE Road near Kengeri Exit Toll due to the use of the motorcycle No.
KA-01-JB-5560 and car No. KA-05-MW-0304 accident taken place resulting in the injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:

In the evidence affidavit petitioner stated that in the accident he has suffered fracture of neck of left femur, acetabulam fracture of posterior column, fracture of both bones of left leg, took treatment at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital as an inpatient for 12 days, 9 days and 9 days respectively at the cost of Rs.1,25,000/- and as on the date of accident use to earn Rs.40,000/- per annum by working as coolie.
18.
In the written statement respondent No.1 and 2 denied the allegation regarding the nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

In the cross-examination PW.1 denied the suggestion about non-production of documents regarding spending of Rs.1,25,000/- for treatment,
nourishment etc.
The petitioner denied the suggestion that he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.

19. In the evidence affidavit PW.2 Dr. Nagaraj.B.N. stated that on 29.03.2023 when clinically examined the petitioner noticed that petitioner suffered disability at 83% to lower limb which is about 28% to whole body.
In the evidence PW.2 produced clinical report and X-ray at Ex.P11 and Ex.P12.
In the cross-examination PW.2 stated that he never treated the petitioner after 4 years of the accident during 2023 clinically examined the petitioner.
PW.2 stated that fractures of tibia of the petitioner are united and up to 05.02.2022 petitioner was under treatment.
PW.2 admitted that in Ex.P8 Discharge Summary nothing has been mentioned about non-union of fractures.

20. Wound Certificate, Discharge Summaries, medical bills, X-ray and other documents shows that in the accident petitioner suffered fracture of neck of left femur, fracture of acetabulam fracture of posterior column, fracture of both bones of left leg, took treatment at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital,
Bengaluru as an inpatient from 28.1.2019 to 08.2.2019, 09.9.2019, 18.9.2019 at the cost of Rs.16,100/-.

In the copy of the Adhar Card marked at Ex.P7 date of birth of the petitioner is noted as 10.4.1988.
21.
In this case, the petitioner has not produced documents regarding his occupation and income.
In the file, there are no evidence to show either loss of income or decrease in the income of the petitioner subsequent to the treatment taken for the injuries suffered in the accident.

Hence I have inferred that oral evidence placed by PW.2 Dr.Nagaraj.B.N. is insufficient to award compensation under the head of decrease or loss of income subsequent to the treatment taken for the injuries suffered in the accident.

22. Considering the nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the accident, length, place,
nature of the treatment taken by the petitioner, occupation and status of the petitioner, I award Rs.80,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.16,100/- towards treatment, Rs.25,000/- towards attendant, conveyance, nourishment, Rs.20,000/- towards loss of income during treatment period Swamy vs Pradeep Kumar.

K on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55407070/
4 of the petitioner (6 months) and Rs.70,000/- towards loss of amenities and future unhappiness.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle to Rs.2,11,100/- with current and future interest @ 6% p.a., as compensation.
23.
In the written statement, respondent No.2 insurance company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to car No. KA-05-MW-0304 as on the date of accident.
In the file, there are no evidence to show that as on the date of accident, respondent No.1 owner of the car has violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being owner and insurer of the car No. KA-05-MW-0304 are liable to pay compensation and award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 163-A of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.
The respondents No.1 and 2 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.2,11,100/- with current and future interest @ 6% p.a., to the petitioner as compensation.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the car No.KA- 05-MW-0304 shall deposit compensation amount and interest within three months from today.
After deposit of compensation and interest, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.

(Dictated to the Stenographer Gr.I, transcribed by him, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 10 th day of December, 2024)
(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
